description: Start a Live Activity on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island. Use this for work with a start and an end that you will report on while it runs — a build, a deploy, a test or capture run, a batch job, a wash cycle, a charge, a delivery. It is the right surface whenever the operator wants to watch progress without opening anything, and the only one that can be. Always end it. `title`, `kind` and `deepLink` are frozen when it starts and cannot be changed by an update, so anything that must move belongs in the content state fields. Calling this again with an id that is already running restarts it, which is visible to the user.

alert.description: Sends this one push as a visible notification. For state changes worth interrupting someone for — finished, failed — and nothing else; it does not rename the activity.

chart.description: A plot of the number this activity is about — watts climbing, queue depth dropping. Send the whole window on every update. It outranks `progress` for the space, and `items` suppress it entirely on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island.

categories.description: Rich categories aligned with points. Use category signal for meanings that vary per bar, such as favorable off-peak and unfavorable peak periods. The server derives labels.

id.description: Stable category id for the time period or bucket.

label.description: Short display label. The server derives the legacy labels array from categories.

signal.description: Contextual interpretation of this category, such as a favorable off-peak or unfavorable peak period.

labels.description: Optional category labels aligned with points. Small surfaces omit them; large widgets and detail views show a readable subset.

max.description: Pins the top of the plot.

min.description: Pins the bottom of the plot. Without a range the plot scales to the series, so a flat-but-noisy one looks dramatic. Send at least `min: 0` whenever the absolute scale is the point.

points.description: 2-60 values, oldest first, plotted evenly spaced. There are no timestamps: send a fixed rolling window. The small surfaces — Lock Screen, small widget, grid cells — average a long series down to what they can draw, so the window you send is always the window shown; send the resolution the data actually has.

rangeValueLabel.description: Short meaning shared by every supplied ranges[].value marker, such as Daily average, Median, or Current. Omit it rather than guessing.

ranges.description: Two to sixty low/high intervals. The server derives legacy points from each value, or from its midpoint when value is absent.

high.description: Top of the observed or expected interval.

low.description: Bottom of the observed or expected interval.

value.description: Optional representative value marked inside the interval. Its meaning is supplied by the chart's rangeValueLabel; clients never infer one.

reference.description: A target, budget, SLO or threshold, drawn as a dashed rule across the plot. Usually the difference between a trend you can read and one you can act on, because above-or-below needs no axis labels. The rule has no numeric label; when its exact value matters, lead the card's short `subtitle` with its formatted meaning and value.

referenceMetadata.description: Optional label and semantic meaning for the numeric reference. Kept separate so older clients still receive and draw the legacy reference number.

label.description: Short name for the rule, such as Target, Baseline, Budget, or Capacity.

semantic.description: Meaning of the rule. Renderers choose its color, dash, emphasis, and accessibility wording.

flow.description: Whether a quantity flows into or out of the measured system.

role.description: What the series represents; affects emphasis and fill treatment, never a producer-selected color.

signal.description: Contextual interpretation from the producer's perspective, not an intrinsic property of the value.

semantic.description: Meaning shared by a single points or range series and inherited by any multi-series entry that omits a semantic dimension.

flow.description: Whether a quantity flows into or out of the measured system.

role.description: What the series represents; affects emphasis and fill treatment, never a producer-selected color.

signal.description: Contextual interpretation from the producer's perspective, not an intrinsic property of the value.

series.description: One to four semantic series for vertical bars, stacked or grouped when multiple. The server derives legacy points as their totals for older clients.

id.description: Stable series id, used to keep renderer-owned presentation consistent.

points.description: Non-negative values aligned one-for-one with every other series, label, and category.

semantic.description: Optional role, flow, and contextual signal hints. Renderers choose all actual colors and patterns.

flow.description: Whether a quantity flows into or out of the measured system.

role.description: What the series represents; affects emphasis and fill treatment, never a producer-selected color.

signal.description: Contextual interpretation from the producer's perspective, not an intrinsic property of the value.

stacking.description: How multiple bar series share each category: stacked into one column or grouped side by side.

style.description: `line` is a sparkline with a soft area fill; `bar` grows every bar from the bottom of the range; `delta` anchors at zero instead, so signed values grow up or down from a zero rule; `range` draws floating low/high intervals with optional publisher-defined value markers.

countdownGranularity.description: How the `endsAt` countdown reads. `second` (default) keeps the native ticking clock; `minute` renders a rounded estimate like ~12 min and updates locally at minute boundaries. Ignored without `endsAt`.

deepLink.description: HTTPS URL opened when the activity is tapped. FROZEN at start, like `title` and `kind`.

endsAt.description: When the run is expected to finish. iOS then renders a countdown from the device clock, so you do not need to publish updates just to tick time forward. Prefer this over server-ticked percentages.

externalActivityId.description: Your own id for this run. It addresses the activity on every later update and on the end call, so keep it until the end returns 2xx. Starting on an id that is already running RESTARTS it: the running activity is ended and a new one replaces it, which the user sees as one dismissing and another animating in. That is how to change a frozen `title`, `kind` or `deepLink`, and it is not something to do on a tick.

icon.description: SF Symbol name, overriding the one `kind` implies.

items.description: Up to 6 rows, for an activity that is several things at once — three chargers, a queue of jobs, a set of checks. Rows REPLACE the progress bar and SUPPRESS any `chart` on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island, silently and with no error, so send items or a chart but not both.

icon.description: SF Symbol name for this row.

id.description: Stable id for this row, unique within the activity.

semantic.description: Optional role and flow hints for this row. `status` remains its health/lifecycle meaning.

flow.description: Whether this item flows into or out of the measured system.

role.description: What this item represents. Renderers choose the emphasis; producers never choose a color.

status.description: Rows with `finished` or `offline` are hidden, and the activity counts the rest as its active total.

statusIcon.description: A second SF Symbol for what this row is doing right now, drawn beside its own icon — arrow.up while charging, pause.fill while held.

subtitle.description: A second line under the row's title.

value.description: The row's reading, as a display string.

kind.description: Picks the default glyph when no `icon` is set: generic, progress, charging, appliance, job, timer. Frozen once the activity starts.

progress.description: Progress bar, 0-1. A `chart` outranks it for the space, and `items` replace it entirely.

relevanceScore.description: How this activity ranks against others in Smart Stack on the Lock Screen and Apple Watch; higher wins, with no fixed ceiling. Start low on a long run and raise it as the activity becomes urgent.

signal.description: Contextual meaning of the activity's current state. It changes the renderer-owned accent, symbol, and accessibility wording without changing the free-form state text.

staleAt.description: After this iOS renders the activity as out of date, so a run whose producer has gone quiet says so instead of looking current. Send it on every push, a little past when you next expect to publish. It is the only thing that makes a stalled producer visible to the operator, and it costs nothing when you do keep publishing.

state.description: Free-form short text for where the run is up to — "running", "Rinse", "waiting for approval". Rendered as text; no value has special meaning, and setting it to "finished" does not end the activity.

statusIcon.description: A second SF Symbol for what the activity is doing right now, drawn beside the main one — bolt.fill while boosting, exclamationmark.triangle.fill when something needs attention. Unlike `icon`, which says what the activity IS, this says what it is DOING, so it is content state and changes on every update.

subtitle.description: A line of prose under the title. Updatable.

title.description: The name of the thing. FROZEN for the life of the activity — no update can change what the Lock Screen shows, only a restart can. So it must never carry a value that moves: "CI build #1234" and "Dishwasher" are titles, "42 min left" and "64% charged" are not. Put those in `value`, `progress` or `endsAt`.

value.description: The headline, as a display string. With `items`, an explicit value outranks the derived active-item count.

name: start_live_activity

activityInstanceId.description: The server's id for this exact activity.

apnsId.description: APNs' own id for the push.

reason.description: APNs failure reason, when it failed.

status.description: The HTTP status APNs answered with; 200 is delivered.

pushToStartAttempted.description: How many devices were sent the push that starts the activity. ZERO means nobody will see this one, or anything else you publish: the operator has no device registered, so tell them to open the 00Widget app and allow notifications rather than continuing to publish.

pushToStartPrunedStale.description: Devices that had not run the app in 30 days, so were not sent the start and were removed. They return on their own the next time the app launches.

pushToStartRecentlyActive.description: Of the devices sent the start, how many have run the 00Widget app in the last 7 days. Fewer than `pushToStartAttempted` means some were sent it and may never show it; compare `registeredDevices` on your next update.

restarted.description: True when an activity was already running under this id, so it was ended and replaced rather than started fresh. The user saw one dismiss and another animate in.

warnings.description: Advisory notes about how this activity will RENDER, on a call that otherwise succeeded. Empty when there is nothing to say. These never affect whether the request worked; act on them anyway, because the operator's Lock Screen is the one thing you cannot look at.

title: Start a Live Activity
